docs.title: Quick Start Overview
docs.text:
Welcome to HWMARS — Hardware Measurement and Attestation Roots for RISC-V.

HWMARS is an open hardware framework for building and experimenting with hardware-based MARS implementations using LiteX, Secworks SHA-256, and RISC-V on FPGA.

docs.title: What HWMARS provides
docs.text: ✅ Modular Measurement Root (MRoT) in SystemVerilog ✅ Real Secworks SHA-256 integration via AXI-Stream ✅ DMAReader path for memory → SHA stream ✅ Attestation Root (ARoT) using Ed25519 (stub, replaceable) ✅ RISC-V firmware that emits EAT/CBOR attestation tokens

docs.title: Hardware & Tools
docs.text: Component Description FPGA Digilent Arty A7-35T (Artix-7) CPU core VexRiscv (LiteX) Crypto IP Secworks SHA-256 core Framework LiteX SoC builder Firmware RISC-V bare-metal C Attestation CBOR-encoded EAT tokens

docs.text: You can run the platform either in simulation or on the Arty A7-35T FPGA.

docs.title: Build SoC
docs.text: ```bash cd hwmars/soc python build_mars_sim.py

docs.title: This builds a LiteX system with:
docs.text:
VexRiscv CPU

MRoT + Secworks SHA-256 stream wrapper

Ed25519 signer (stub)

DMAReader for streaming memory → MRoT

Build firmware make -C ../firmware

Run simulation litex_sim --ram-init ../firmware/main.bin

docs.title: Expected UART output:
docs.text:
HWMARSE (Secworks SHA-256 + DMA) agg: 5F34B02D0C...E093AF EAT (hex): A4646E6F6E6365... Done.

⚙️ Option B — Arty A7-35T Hardware Generate the SoC cd mars-litex-arty-secworks/soc python build_arty_mars_soc.py

(set run=True inside the script if you want Vivado to build the bitstream automatically)

Compile firmware make -C ../firmware

Program the board

Connect Arty A7 via USB.

Program bitstream (.bit) via Vivado or litex_term.

Upload and execute firmware:

litex_term COM3 --kernel ../firmware/main.bin

✅ Verify output

UART (115200 8N1) should display:

MARS/EMBRAVE (Secworks SHA-256 + DMA) agg: <32-byte digest> EAT (hex): Done.

You now have a working attestation path using real SHA-256 hardware.

docs.title: DMA Measurement Demo
docs.text: HWMARS supports hardware-driven measurement using a LiteX DMAReader streaming data into the Secworks SHA-256 engine.

docs.title: Interactive from BIOS
docs.text:
```text lite> mem_write mrot_dma_base 0x40000000 lite> mem_write mrot_dma_length 256 lite> mem_write mrot_dma_start 1 The MRoT hashes 256 bytes from memory and asserts done.

Python RemoteClient Example python Copy code from litex import RemoteClient wb = RemoteClient(); wb.open()

wb.regs.mrot_dma_base.write(0x40000000) wb.regs.mrot_dma_length.write(256) wb.regs.mrot_dma_start.write(1) while wb.regs.mrot_dma_busy.read(): pass print("DMA measurement complete.") wb.close()

The digest is aggregated and signed to form an EAT (Entity Attestation Token).

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: HWMARS integrates hardware and firmware components to realize Measurement and Attestation Roots (MARS) on RISC-V FPGA.

docs.title: Attestation flow
docs.text: Memory → DMA → MRoT (SHA-256) → Digest → ARoT (sign) → UART (EAT)

docs.title: Firmware Overview
docs.text: The RISC-V firmware (firmware/main.c) orchestrates measurement, aggregation, signing, and token generation.

docs.title: Main tasks
docs.text:
1. Trigger MRoT measurement (manual or DMA)
  2. Aggregate digests
  3. Invoke signer (Ed25519)
  4. Build CBOR-encoded EAT token
  5. Output via UART

docs.title: Output Example
docs.text:
HWMARS (Secworks SHA-256 + DMA) agg: 4A89BFF2...DE05 EAT (hex): A4646E6F6E6365...736967 Done.

docs.title: “404 Not Found” on mkdocs serve
docs.text: → Ensure docs/index.md exists.

docs.title: “sha256_core” missing in Vivado
docs.text: → Add the Secworks core under rtl/secworks/.

docs.title: UART gibberish
docs.text: → Use 115200 8N1 baud, disable flow control.

docs.title: DMA never finishes
docs.text: → Ensure length is multiple of 4 bytes.
